gaps.fact: Vitis riparia as one of the North American species grown in Canada beside labrusca: the Codex names riparia only as a rootstock parent; no chapter or question presents it as a Canadian vine species.

Sparkling wine as one of Canada's three styles: only the country record mentions it (Sparkling Icewine, Nova Scotia's traditional method estate, Chardonnay as sparkling base); neither chapter and no question does.

Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer as Canadian whites: Pinot Gris stands only in the country record's grapes, Gewürztraminer nowhere for Canada; the Village chapter says only aromatic whites. Chardonnay, the Introductory cell's other white, is likewise taught only in the country record.
Pinot Noir, Merlot and Cabernet Franc as Canada's red table wines: only the country record's grapes name them; neither chapter does, and c-6w1pultw speaks of Bordeaux reds without a grape.

Canada has no national wine law and each province writes its own rules: the country record teaches it (overview; trap 4), but the Régionale chapter presents VQA without saying it is provincial, and no question asks it.

Ontario makes about half of all Canadian wine and 90 per cent of its icewine, and the Okanagan sits on the fiftieth parallel: the Codex says only the larger producer, most of the country's icewine and close to fifty degrees north; no figure is taught or asked.
Canada as the world's leading icewine producer, the fruit often picked in the middle of the night: neither point appears anywhere in the Codex.

Commercial wine since the middle of the nineteenth century, Prohibition from 1916 to 1927, and the first new Ontario winery licence of the 1970s: only the 1975 licence (Inniskillin, the first since 1929) is taught, in the country record; neither chapter carries any of it and no question asks it.
Sweet and savoury pairings with icewine, the Court's Certified pairing cell: nothing in the Codex pairs icewine with food.

errors.where: js/data-regions.js, REGIONS.countries.canada.questions r-fyn9xj6a, exp: "Germany's Eiswein rule is minus 7°C, the figure most often swapped in."
errors.claim: German law sets minus 7°C as the temperature for picking Eiswein.
errors.correction: German wine law fixes no temperature: the grapes must be frozen when picked and pressed, at Beerenauslese must weight, and minus 7°C is guidance. The Codex's own ice-wine technique puts it that way (German guidance gives minus 7°C for Eiswein harvesting and pressing in a frozen condition). The line should say that German guidance uses minus 7°C while Canada writes minus 8°C into law. The same law framing recurs in the germany index (REGIONS.countries.germany.questions, exp: "The law asks for minus 7 °C or colder at picking and pressing"), for the owner to weigh with the Germany and Sweet Wines subjects.
errors.source: German wine law's definition of Eiswein (grapes frozen at harvest and pressing, no temperature named); js/regions/techniques.json, ice-wine; the Court's own sweet wine and Germany cells say only that the grapes must be frozen

courtUpdates.now: Ontario Regulation 359/24, filed 13 September 2024, reorganised the Niagara Peninsula's terms and created West Niagara as a regional appellation over the sub-appellations west of the Welland Canal, beside Niagara-on-the-Lake and the Niagara Escarpment; the canada country record already teaches the three (card 5; ladder).
courtUpdates.source: Ontario Regulation 359/24 under the Vintners Quality Alliance Act, 1999 (ontario.ca/laws/regulation/R24359)

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 0 (no Régionale category carries Canada; its Canadian stems, i-whkcs973, i-4dov377v, i-abpix1eg and i-kx5sqw0v, sit in world categories) and Village 33 (Pacific NW, NY & Canada, of which 6 are Canadian: c-9w6hed70, c-6w1pultw, c-z4bknzgb, c-9ljj13hh, c-atb8n93b, c-sbso69yj), 33 in all, 10 Canadian stems across both banks with c-ep6h3a2y. Icewine is taught to the Court's depth and beyond (minus 8 degrees, 35 Brix, natural freezing, Vidal), and VQA, the 1988 pull-out and the southern Okanagan benches are asked. Everything else the Court lists is thin: the grape lists, Canada's sparkling wine, the provincial nature of the law, Ontario's shares, the history row and the icewine pairing are taught in the country record at best and never asked. The Court prints Inniskillen; the house is Inniskillin, as the Codex spells it, and the Court's text stands as printed. One error, at medium confidence: the canada record's question r-fyn9xj6a calls minus 7°C Germany's Eiswein rule, where German law names no temperature; the Canadian facts themselves (minus 8°C, 35 Brix, natural freezing, Vidal) are sound. Two searches spent, both on the Niagara appellations: West Niagara is confirmed by the 2024 regulation (logged above); whether that regulation also places St. David's Bench under the Niagara Escarpment as well as Niagara-on-the-Lake could not be confirmed from the fragments found, so the canada record's placement of St. David's Bench under Niagara-on-the-Lake alone is left for the owner to check against the regulation's text.
